leagues.name: Women's Super League
notes: 2026/27 is the first WSL season with 14 clubs, expanded from 12: Birmingham City (WSL2 champions), Crystal Palace (runners-up) and Charlton Athletic (play-off winners) were promoted; no club was relegated in 2025/26.
Title-sponsored by Barclays since 2019/20; Sky Sports shows the league from 2025/26 under a five-year UK broadcast deal.
Run by WSL Football, a company split from the FA.

claims.text: Amnesty International's British head of campaigns, Felix Jakens, warned that Rwanda is using its Aston Villa sponsorship to sportswash a record of arbitrary detention, torture and repression of free speech, and is fuelling conflict in eastern Congo through its support for M23 rebels and its military's actions there.
claims.short: Amnesty: Villa's Visit Rwanda deal is sportswashing

proposedRatings.reasoning: Visit Rwanda moves to the FRONT of the Aston Villa Women shirt in 2026/27 (SportsPro, 15 Jul 2026), replacing Betano. The Rwandan government, its owner, is already rated severe on the existing claims (UN experts: 3,000-4,000 Rwandan troops fighting alongside M23; conflict-mineral levies). Amnesty International publicly called this specific deal sportswashing (Morning Star/PA, 15 Jul 2026). Existing severe tier carries over; the new Amnesty claim strengthens it. Existing sponsor, no re-rating needed - proposal only confirms the tier.

Etihad stays on the front of the Manchester City Women shirt (CFG partnership page; the women's team plays at the Etihad Campus). Owner is Abu Dhabi's government, which sits behind the UAE mass trial claims. Existing serious tier carries over.

Emirates renewed to 2033 and stays on the front of the Arsenal Women shirt per the men's renewal coverage; owner is Dubai's government via Investment Corporation of Dubai, with the 2024 UAE mass-trial claim. Existing serious tier carries over. Women's-team-specific confirmation of the front placement is still open.
Barclays is the WSL title sponsor (home.barclays), so it is a league partner for all 14 clubs. Its existing concern tier (banking conduct record) carries over to the WSL context.

unsourced: CONFLICT - Christopher Ward sleeve placement at Charlton: the Wikipedia 2026-27 WSL table lists Christopher Ward on the Charlton Women sleeve, but the club's own announcements say Christopher Ward appears on the left sleeve of the MEN'S first-team shirts only (2026/27 Reebok home kit reveal, 2 Jul 2026, https://www.cafc.co.uk/news/202627-reebok-home-kit-revealed; away kit reveal, 19 Aug 2026, https://www.cafc.co.uk/news/202627-reebok-away-kit-revealed). No Christopher Ward entry was added for the women's team.

CONFLICT - GGM Gastro placement wording: the Wikipedia table lists 'shorts'; the club announcement (10 Oct 2025) says the brand mark features 'on the back of the shorts worn by Everton Women', so it was recorded as placement 'shorts' per the primary source.

Brighton Women: Pinterest back-of-shirt placement from the Wikipedia table; American Express front and Experience Kissimmee sleeve match the men's 2026-27 kit but the women's-specific announcement was not located.
Crystal Palace Women: Temporal front and Tsakos Energy Navigation sleeve from the Wikipedia table; no primary announcement located.

Liverpool Women: Standard Chartered front, Expedia sleeve and LFC Foundation back from the Wikipedia table; no women's-specific announcement located. The LFC Foundation back-of-shirt article found via sitemap is the 2023-24 men's European-games deal, not a women's placement.
Tottenham Women: e.l.f. back-of-shirt placement from the Wikipedia table, unverified; AIA front carried from the men's kit (the Kraken announcement does not restate AIA).

Manchester City Women: Etihad front is confirmed at club/CFG level but the CFG page does not name the women's team; Revolut back and Joie shorts placements from the Wikipedia table. Joie women's-team partnership since March 2023 is sourced (MEN via Wayback), but the shorts placement specifically is not.
Chelsea Women: the Circle front, Škoda back and Here We Flo back-of-shorts placements are now verified on chelseafc.com partner pages; the exact start date of the Here We Flo deal is not stated.
WTW as a WSL major partner: wslfootball.com footer lists it, but wtwco.com's WSL page could not be fetched (403/429) to confirm the partnership scope.

Nike as WSL league-wide kit supplier, plus minor league partners Football Manager and Panini, and major partners Airbnb, Mercedes-Benz: visible in the wslfootball.com homepage footer tiers but individual partnership pages were not all fetched.
Arsenal Women: Emirates front and Deel sleeve are taken from the men's-team deal reporting and the Wikipedia table; no Arsenal Women-specific kit announcement located.

Kit manufacturer for most WSL women's teams (Adidas/Nike/Puma/Macron/Castore/New Balance/Reebok per the Wikipedia table) - manufacturers are not yet represented in the kit data; recorded here as text. The Charlton 2026/27 kits are Reebok (club reveal, men's-focused but women's first-teamers modelled the away shirt).

London City Lionesses owner Michele Kang's Kynisca structure: the club announcement quotes Kang but the corporate chain (Kynisca Sports International LLC, USA) is from press coverage of her multi-club group, not from a filing.
Lilley Plummer Risks ownership: SportsMint reports it was acquired by Goldman Sachs in 2024; no filing checked, so no ownerId was set.

WSL 2026-27 shirt placements for brighton-and-hove-albion-w, crystal-palace-w and liverpool-w: only empty kit shells (no sponsors listed) because the placements were found only as Wikipedia table leads with no primary source openable. Kits can be filled when club announcements are cited.

Kit makers new-balance (West Ham W) and reebok (Charlton W from 2026/27) were researched but the women's shirts are unverified as to manufacturer (Versus/club reveals cover the men's kits); no sponsor entries created.
